extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers (especially early-career and practicing reviewers) in health and biomedical research
extracted.subtask_short: peer review training for health research
extracted.subtask_description: A curated toolkit and bibliography of training materials, checklists, reporting guidelines and ethical standards to help reviewers learn how to decide on, perform, and re-review manuscripts in health research. Focus is on building reviewer skills (including statistical review) and using reporting guidelines appropriate to study type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding whether to accept a review (take on a review)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to evaluate whether you should take on a particular review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the manuscript fits your expertise, whether you can provide an objective assessment (conflicts of interest), and whether you can complete the review within the journal's timeframe; weigh benefits vs. time costs. (Page phrase: 'how to evaluate whether you should take on a particular review')

rubrics_metrics.name: How to approach the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to approach the review process and structure a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a systematic approach (e.g., scope, methodology, results, interpretation, reporting), be constructive and specific, and use appropriate checklists and reporting guidelines to assess completeness. (Page phrase: 'how to approach the review')

rubrics_metrics.name: How to re-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on re-reviewing a revised manuscript after initial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that authors have addressed prior concerns, evaluate adequacy of revisions and any new issues introduced, and confirm that reporting meets applicable guidelines. (Page phrase: 'how to ... re-review')

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines for peer reviewers (COPE guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee on Publication Ethics' ethical guidelines for peer reviewers detailing reviewers’ responsibilities at all stages of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow COPE principles such as confidentiality, declaring conflicts of interest, providing unbiased and constructive feedback, and acting with integrity throughout the review process. (Page: 'The Committee on Publication Ethics published ... ethical guidelines for peer reviewers ... detailing peer reviewers’ responsibilities at all stages of the review process.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Use critical appraisal checklists (CASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use checklists to guide your peer review of different study types provided by Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the checklist appropriate to the study design (e.g., RCT, cohort, qualitative) to systematically assess validity, bias, and applicability. (Page: 'The Critical Appraisal Skills Programme offers checklists to guide your peer review of different study types.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical peer review: CHAMP Statement and checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: The CHAMP Statement and checklist developed for statistical peer review of medical papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CHAMP checklist to evaluate statistical methods, reporting of analyses, assumptions, handling of missing data, and appropriateness of inferences. (Page: 'The CHAMP Statement and checklist ... have been developed for statistical peer review of medical papers.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competencies and skills for peer reviewers (Web of Science / Publons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical peer review courses that teach core competencies and skills needed for peer review (originally Publons Academy; now Web of Science Academy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop skills such as critical appraisal, constructive commentary, ethical conduct, and clear reporting of concerns and recommendations. Use practice reviews and coursework to build competence. (Page: 'offers practical peer review courses ... to teach you the core competencies and skills needed for peer review.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of training materials and practice reviews (BMJ, BMC, Elsevier, Springer, Taylor & Francis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with available training packages (e.g., BMJ PowerPoints and practice reviews, BMC blog series, Elsevier/Springer/Nature/Taylor & Francis guides) to learn reviewing best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete tutorials and practice review exercises to learn structure, tone, and expectations of good peer reviews; adopt publisher-specific guidance where relevant. (Page lists multiple publisher training resources.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Check whether journals ask reviewers to use reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that journals may include instructions to reviewers about reporting guidelines — EQUATOR research found ~35% of journals offered online instructions and about half of those mentioned reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult the journal's reviewer instructions and apply any requested reporting guidelines when assessing manuscripts. (Page: 'around 35% of journals offered ... instructions ... about peer review ... of those, about half mentioned reporting guidelines.')

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT (randomised trials) and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT is the reporting guideline for randomised trials; extensions cover specific trial types and reporting elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For RCTs, use CONSORT to check completeness of trial reporting (randomisation, allocation concealment, blinding, participant flow, outcomes). Consider relevant CONSORT extensions. (Listed under 'Reporting guidelines for main study types: Randomised trials — CONSORT Extensions')

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE (observational studies) and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE is the reporting guideline for observational studies; extensions cover specific designs or topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STROBE to assess reporting of cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies (participants, variables, bias, statistical methods). (Page: 'Observational studies — STROBE Extensions')

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA (systematic reviews) and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA is the reporting guideline for systematic reviews with extensions for various review types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess search strategy transparency, study selection flow, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, and synthesis reporting using PRISMA and relevant extensions. (Page: 'Systematic reviews — PRISMA Extensions')

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT and PRISMA-P (study protocols)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT and PRISMA-P are reporting guidelines for study protocols and protocol reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether protocols report rationale, objectives, design, methods, outcomes, sample size and analysis plans clearly and completely. (Page: 'Study protocols — SPIRIT PRISMA-P')

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD and TRIPOD (diagnostic/prognostic studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: STARD (diagnostic accuracy studies) and TRIPOD (prediction model development and validation) reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check completeness of reporting of diagnostic/prognostic methods, participant selection, index/reference tests, model development and validation, and performance measures. (Page: 'Diagnostic/prognostic studies — STARD TRIPOD')

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE (case reports) and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: CARE is the reporting guideline for clinical case reports (and extensions where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and completeness of case descriptions, diagnostic reasoning, interventions, outcomes, and lessons learned. (Page: 'Case reports — CARE Extensions')

rubrics_metrics.name: AGREE and RIGHT (clinical practice guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: AGREE and RIGHT are instruments/guidelines for reporting and appraising clinical practice guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AGREE/RIGHT to evaluate guideline development methods, evidence appraisal, stakeholder involvement, clarity, and applicability. (Page: 'Clinical practice guidelines — AGREE RIGHT')

rubrics_metrics.name: SRQR and COREQ (qualitative research)
rubrics_metrics.description: SRQR and COREQ are reporting guidelines for qualitative research studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reporting of research paradigm, sampling, data collection, analysis methods, researcher reflexivity, and evidence supporting interpretations. (Page: 'Qualitative research — SRQR COREQ')

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE (animal pre-clinical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARRIVE is the reporting guideline for animal pre-clinical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that animal studies report experimental design, randomisation, blinding, sample size calculations, outcomes and welfare considerations. (Page: 'Animal pre-clinical studies — ARRIVE')

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE (quality improvement studies) and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE is the reporting guideline for quality improvement studies, with extensions where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether QI reports describe context, interventions, measures, analysis and sustainability. (Page: 'Quality improvement studies — SQUIRE Extensions')

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS (economic evaluations) and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: CHEERS is the reporting guideline for economic evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CHEERS to assess clarity of cost/effectiveness methods, perspective, time horizon, model structure, and uncertainty analyses. (Page: 'Economic evaluations — CHEERS Extensions')

rubrics_metrics.name: Use blogs, debates and community resources for perspective and tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Community-authored blog posts, debates, and popular-press pieces provide pragmatic tips and perspectives on peer review (examples cited include posts by individual academics, Nature's Peer Review Debate, The Guardian, and Sense about Science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult experienced reviewers' posts and debate summaries for practical tips and common pitfalls, but cross-check recommendations with formal guidance and journal policies. (Page lists multiple blog/press items and events such as Peer Review Week.)
